title: When the Parish Turns
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Voss is exhumed for a land dispute and found empty, hotel concierge Petra Okonkwo realizes she saw a stranger sign the guestbook under Voss's name three days earlier — meaning the founder may never have died. As Petra investigates, she uncovers that half the parish, including the sheriff and her own brother, helped fake Voss's death to protect him from prosecution for an old crime. The 'dead witness' everyone fears is Voss himself, hiding in her hotel, and finding him means choosing between exposing the town's beloved lie and protecting the people she loves. In the end, Petra forces a public confession that convicts no one but frees everyone — and Voss walks out of the parish alive, leaving the truth behind like a coat he no longer needs.
about_author: Oscar Okafor is a former night-desk clerk at a coastal inn who spent a decade listening to guests lie beautifully. He writes mysteries about the quiet crimes ordinary communities commit together.

chapters.title: The Guestbook Lie
chapters.summary: Petra Okonkwo, concierge at the Marlowe Grand, notices a gaunt man signing in as 'E. Voss' — a name belonging to the town's founder, dead eleven years. Her curiosity is professional, not personal, until the man leaves a tip folded into a shape she recognizes from her childhood. POV: Petra. Beat: unease disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Exhumation Day
chapters.summary: A property lawsuit forces the exhumation of Edmund Voss before a crowd of half the parish. The coffin is empty except for sandbags and a funeral program printed on paper that didn't exist until two years after his burial. Sheriff Dane Colter shuts it down fast — too fast. POV: Petra. Beat: the ground opens and nothing makes sense.

chapters.title: Everyone Knew But Me
chapters.summary: Petra canvasses mourners from the old funeral and finds every account of Voss's open casket contradicts the others. Her brother Theo, the parish sexton, goes pale when she mentions the empty grave and begs her to drop it. POV: Petra. Beat: loyalty begins to feel like a wall built around her.

chapters.title: Room 214
chapters.summary: Petra checks the hotel ledger against keycard logs and finds Room 214 occupied off-book for six weeks, paid in cash by Sheriff Colter himself. She enters while cleaning and finds medicine, a Bible with Voss's handwriting, and a photograph of the parish from 1979 with one face scratched out. POV: Petra. Beat: the hunt becomes intimate.

chapters.title: What the Founder Buried
chapters.summary: Digging through archives, Petra learns Voss built the town on mill money that vanished along with his business partner, Amara Diallo, who was declared dead the same winter. The scratched-out face in the photo is Diallo's. POV: Petra. Beat: the beloved founder curdles into something complicated.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Warning
chapters.summary: Colter corners Petra at the hotel bar, courteous and terrifying, telling her the parish buried its grief once already and she shouldn't make them do it twice. That night someone keys her car and leaves a funeral lily on the windshield. POV: Petra. Beat: fear arrives wearing Sunday clothes.

chapters.title: Theo's Silence
chapters.summary: Petra confronts Theo, who admits he dug the grave empty on orders he never questioned because Voss once saved him from prison. Their fight cracks something old between them — Petra has always been the one who notices; Theo, the one who obeys. POV: Theo (first alternate). Beat: love and duty pull opposite directions.

chapters.title: A Witness Who Won't Stay Dead
chapters.summary: Petra tracks down Diallo's daughter, Ruth, living under another name two counties over. Ruth insists her mother is dead — then slips and says 'she' when describing the person who wrote her last letter. Someone matching Amara Diallo's description checked into a clinic nearby. POV: Petra. Beat: hope and dread in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Clinic File
chapters.summary: Posing as family, Petra gets a glimpse of the patient: an elderly woman, alive, guarded, with Diallo's eyes. Before Petra can speak with her, the woman is discharged early — signed out by a lawyer whose firm has represented the Voss estate for forty years. POV: Petra. Beat: the truth keeps being carried away just ahead of her.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Sundays
chapters.summary: Petra reconstructs the conspiracy: Voss faked his death facing fraud charges, and the parish protected him because his charity kept them fed through the recession. Colter, the priest, the mayor, Theo — a whole congregation of accomplices. POV: Petra. Beat: justice outside the law starts looking like the law's failure first.

chapters.title: The Man in 214 Speaks
chapters.summary: Voss finally reveals himself to Petra, frail and unrepentant and strangely kind, admitting he sent for her because she was the only person who'd notice everything and still keep a secret. He claims Amara betrayed him first. POV: Voss. Beat: the monster turns out to be human, which is worse.

chapters.title: Ruth's Grief
chapters.summary: Ruth tells Petra what really happened in 1979: Voss stole the mill, let Amara take the blame, and she fled rather than hang for his crime. Ruth came back not for money but to make him say her mother's name out loud, once, in front of the town. POV: Ruth. Beat: revenge revealed as a hunger for acknowledgment.

chapters.title: Colter's Confession
chapters.summary: Sheriff Colter breaks: he's been sheltering Voss for years out of gratitude and shame, and now the exhumation has made concealment impossible. He gives Petra until Sunday service to decide what she'll do — and warns that if Voss falls, the town falls with him. POV: Colter. Beat: duty and loyalty tear down the middle.

chapters.title: The Fire at the Archive
chapters.summary: The county records office burns overnight, destroying the 1979 mill documents. Petra finds accelerant residue matching supplies bought with the church's account number. Someone inside the conspiracy is escalating — and it isn't Voss, who is too sick to leave his room. POV: Petra. Beat: the cover-up develops a life of its own.

chapters.title: Brother Against Knowing
chapters.summary: Evidence points to Theo, who had archive access. Petra covers for him during questioning, lying to police for the first time in her life, then demands the truth. Theo confesses only to burning a duplicate file — to protect Voss, or maybe to protect Petra from what it contained. POV: Theo. Beat: Petra crosses her own line and hates how easily she crossed it.

chapters.title: Amara Comes Home
chapters.summary: Amara Diallo, alive and dying, returns to the parish openly, checking into the Marlowe Grand under her real name. The lobby freezes. She asks Petra for one thing: a room with a view of the church, and a promise that no one will be told she's there until Sunday. POV: Amara. Beat: the dead witness walks in through the front door.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra spends the night keeping two dying enemies apart on different floors, passing messages, refusing to choose. Voss offers her money to keep Amara away; Amara offers her nothing but the truth. By dawn Petra understands she was never investigating a crime — she was being recruited into a verdict. POV: Petra. Beat: the weight of being the only neutral party.

chapters.title: Sunday Service
chapters.summary: The parish gathers, and Petra walks in with both Voss and Amara. In front of God and the town, Amara tells what happened in 1979, and Voss — wheezing, terrified, finally honest — confirms every word and asks forgiveness from no one. Colter arrests no one, because nearly everything is past the statute of limitations. POV: Petra. Beat: climax — truth spoken aloud, and the strange anticlimax of legal mercy.

chapters.title: What the Law Can't Hold
chapters.summary: The arson remains chargeable, and evidence points somewhere unexpected: not Theo, but the mayor's son, who burned the records to hide his own embezzlement from the Voss charities. Colter arrests him cleanly, redeeming a fraction of his badge. POV: Colter. Beat: real justice, small and late, still counts.

chapters.title: Two Deathbeds
chapters.summary: Amara and Voss, both failing, meet once more in the hotel garden — no accusations left, just two old people tallying what a lifetime cost. Amara dies on Thursday with Ruth holding her hand; Voss lives long enough to hear the bell toll for her and weep. POV: Petra. Beat: grief without absolution.

chapters.title: The Empty Grave Filled
chapters.summary: The parish reburies the coffin, this time holding Amara's ashes beside the headstone that bore Voss's name — corrected, at Ruth's insistence, to tell the truth in stone. Theo and Petra stand together at the graveside, their rift scarred over but not healed. POV: Theo. Beat: reconciliation as repair, not restoration.

chapters.title: Concierge, Still Noticing
chapters.summary: Months later, Petra checks in a nervous young couple fleeing something they won't name, and quietly upgrades their room and loses their registration card. Some justice happens outside the law, she thinks, and some of it happens at a front desk. She closes the guestbook on the parish's longest year. POV: Petra. Beat: resolution — mercy chosen freely, at last.
